topics.name: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table

spec_points.description: Describe the relative charges and masses of protons, neutrons, and electrons
Define atomic number, mass number, and isotopes
Describe the arrangement of electrons in shells, sub-shells, and orbitals
Write electron configurations using s, p, d notation
Explain trends in atomic radius, ionisation energy, and electronegativity across periods and down groups
Explain successive ionisation energies and their relationship to electronic structure
Describe properties and reactions of elements in Groups 1, 2, and 7
Describe ionic bonding and the formation of ionic compounds
Describe covalent bonding (including co-ordinate/dative covalent bonds)
Describe metallic bonding and its relationship to physical properties
Predict the shape of molecules using VSEPR theory
Describe van der Waals forces, permanent dipole-dipole forces, and hydrogen bonding
Explain the anomalous properties of water in terms of hydrogen bonding
Explain trends in boiling points of molecules in terms of intermolecular forces
Use the concept of the mole and Avogadro's constant
Calculate molar masses; convert between mass, moles, and number of particles
Calculate amounts using the ideal gas equation pV = nRT
Perform reacting quantities calculations using balanced equations
Calculate percentage yield and atom economy
Define standard enthalpy changes: formation, combustion, neutralisation
Apply Hess's law and use energy cycles (Born-Haber at A2 level)
Use bond enthalpies to estimate ΔH for reactions
Calculate enthalpy changes from calorimetry data using q = mcΔT

modules.name: Application of Core Principles of Chemistry

spec_points.description: Define rate of reaction; describe factors affecting rate
Explain collision theory and the effect of temperature on rate
Draw and interpret Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curves
Explain the role of catalysts in lowering activation energy
Explain dynamic equilibrium and Le Chatelier's principle
Write expressions for Kc and calculate values with units
Explain how changes in temperature, pressure, and concentration affect Kc
Apply equilibrium principles to the Haber process and Contact process
Understand nomenclature: IUPAC naming of alkanes, alkenes, halogenoalkanes, alcohols
Distinguish between homologous series, functional groups, structural isomers
Explain E/Z (cis/trans) isomerism in alkenes
Describe free radical substitution of alkanes (initiation, propagation, termination)
Describe electrophilic addition to alkenes (mechanism with curly arrows)
Explain Markovnikov's rule for addition to unsymmetrical alkenes
Describe the reactions of alkenes with Br₂, HBr, H₂SO₄/H₂O, and H₂
Describe nucleophilic substitution of halogenoalkanes (SN1 and SN2 mechanisms)
Explain elimination reactions of halogenoalkanes
Describe oxidation of primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols with K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄
Describe dehydration of alcohols and esterification
Perform and describe titration procedures with correct technique
Describe procedures for synthesis, purification (recrystallisation, distillation), and characterisation
Identify chemical substances using tests: flame tests, precipitate reactions, gas tests
Determine orders of reaction from experimental data (initial rates and concentration-time graphs)
Write and use rate equations: rate = k[A]^m[B]^n
Use the Arrhenius equation k = Ae^(-Ea/RT); construct and interpret ln k vs 1/T graphs
Propose and test reaction mechanisms consistent with the rate equation
Define Brønsted-Lowry acid and base; identify conjugate pairs
Calculate pH from [H⁺]; use Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 1.0×10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C
Calculate Ka and pKa; distinguish strong and weak acids
Describe buffer solutions and calculate pH of buffers using Ka
Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer and oxidation numbers
Construct half-equations and overall redox equations
Use standard electrode potentials to predict cell EMF and feasibility of reactions
Describe fuel cells and rechargeable batteries
Define transition metals; explain variable oxidation states with examples
Describe the formation of complex ions; use ligand and coordination number terminology
Explain the colour of transition metal complexes in terms of d-orbital splitting
Describe ligand substitution and precipitation reactions of copper and iron complexes
Describe the reactions of aldehydes and ketones: nucleophilic addition, reduction
Distinguish between aldehydes and ketones using Tollens' and Fehling's tests
Describe the reactions of carboxylic acids and esters (esterification, hydrolysis)
Explain the basicity of amines; describe formation of ammonium salts and amides
Describe the properties of amino acids; explain zwitterion formation
Describe the formation and hydrolysis of peptide bonds
Describe addition polymerisation and condensation polymerisation
Interpret mass spectra (molecular ion, base peak, fragmentation patterns)
Interpret NMR spectra: chemical shift, integration, splitting patterns
Plan and carry out multi-step syntheses with appropriate safety precautions
Apply analytical methods (chromatography, spectroscopy) to identify substances
Evaluate experimental procedures and suggest modifications to improve accuracy
